provenance.keySource: A question is authenticated when its printed NTA question id is in the 24-05-2026 (Second) final key for subject 319 and the key option id is one of its four printed option ids. Printed option ids are consecutive per question (2268953069709 to 2268953070048 across the 85 questions).

bankRead: One read-only read on 23 Nov 2026 (SELECT only) with tmp/1123-papers/mathematics/checkA/read_served.mjs, which joins the scratchpad read_bank.mjs (same filter and columns) and the chunked eligibility check (repo readablePracticeQuestions, 40 ids per request) in one run: 395 visible mathematics rows, all 395 pass readablePracticeQuestions (equals the 395 in the stored inventory snapshot computed 22 Nov 2026 21:57 UTC). Served copy: tmp/1123-papers/mathematics/snap/served_rows.json and served_mathematics.json (eligibility output eligible.txt, inventory_snapshot.json).
keyCardDeck: data/keycards/decks/mathematics.json (v7, 548 cards; key_card_suspended was not re-read, the earlier subjects had none suspended). The deck has no cards for the five Applied Mathematics (B2) units and one for Probability Distributions; B2 items can be covered only by bank rows.
syllabusSource: data/cuet_syllabus.js mathematics units (Section A1 common: Algebra, Calculus, Linear Programming, Probability Distributions; B1: Relations and Functions, Vectors and 3D, Probability; B2: Numbers and Quantification, Time Based Data, Inferential Statistics, Financial Mathematics). B2 calculus and matrix items are mapped to the NCERT chapter that teaches them. Every question sits on the 2026 syllabus; Q39 (scalar triple product reading) and Q15 (half-planes of linear inequalities) were doubtful calls kept ON, the stricter reading.
method: data/coverage/METHOD.md (STRICT rule; doubtful = not covered; Key cards count for theory; a numerical needs a served BANK row with the same formula and steps). Type rule written before the search: an item whose answer is a computed value or needs working = numerical; a definition, property, standard result or formula statement = theory. Facts written first: tmp/1123-papers/mathematics/checkA/A_facts_before_search.txt. Search: checkA/s.mjs over the served copy and the deck (whole served bank dumped chapter by chapter in checkA/dump/ and read); builder build_A.mjs checks every cited id.
weakerCalls: Covered with matchKind concept and a weaker call that Checker B should rule on first: Q10 (modulus removal added), Q36 (part B is direct integration only), Q46 (figure reading added to point testing), Q48 (two bank rows together give the two steps), Q67 (algebraic division before integrating), Q74 (bank row works the moving average backwards), Q76 (by elimination: A, B, C taught, D not).
bankRowFlag: Bank row ddbac3ae-10d8-4219-a4d2-6841ebc45f66 (Differential Equations) keys a third-order equation containing sqrt(d2y/dx2) as degree not defined; the CUET 2026 key for Q11 and Q62 clears radicals and gives a degree. The row teaches the opposite of what the paper rewards and was not cited as a match.
paperStructure: One paper of 85 questions, NTA group Core Mathematics and Applied Mathematics: Section A common, mandatory (Q306-320, n 1-15); Section B1 Mathematics (Q321-355, n 16-50); Section B2 Applied Mathematics (Q356-390, n 51-85). A candidate answers A plus one of B1 or B2 (50 questions). No passages, so no item is labelled skill.

facts: A transpose = A, so symmetric; not skew-symmetric, not diagonal
questions.reason: Cards define symmetric, skew-symmetric, diagonal and non-singular, but no served bank row builds a matrix from an element rule, tests it and expands a 3x3 determinant; a numerical needs that bank template.
No served row derives idempotence from AB = A and BA = B; the nearest row only uses A^2 = A as a given.
No served row evaluates a determinant with powers of x by row operations or expansion and reads off its roots.

Bank rows use |adj A| = |A|^(n-1) in the forward direction (|adj A| from |A|) and |kA| = k^n|A|; none goes from |adj A| back to |A| with the two signs, which is the step that gives +-40. Reverse direction, so not covered.

facts: y = sqrt((1 - x)/(1 + x)): log differentiation gives y'/y = -1/(1 - x^2)
questions.reason: The served log-differentiation row is for a variable power (x^sin x); no row differentiates the root of a quotient and rebuilds an expression in y.

facts: f = e^x + e^-x: f' = 0 at x = 0
f'' > 0 there, so minimum value f(0) = 2

matches.teaches: minimum of x + 16/x by g' = 0 and g'' > 0, then the value

questions.reason: Bank row finds the minimum value of a function plus its reciprocal by the first and second derivative test, the same steps with a different function.

facts: f = x/log x: f' = (log x - 1)/(log x)^2
f' > 0 for x > e: increasing on (e, inf)

matches.teaches: finds the interval where a function with log x increases from the sign of f'

questions.reason: Bank row finds an interval of increase from the sign of the derivative of a log function; same steps, the quotient rule is the only change.

facts: Integral of e^x[f(x) + f'(x)] = e^x f(x) + C

matches.teaches: integral of e^x(1/x - 1/x^2) = e^x/x by spotting f + f'
integral of e^x[f + f'] = e^x f + C

questions.reason: Bank row integrates e^x times (f + f') with f = 1/x; the paper uses f = log x - 1/x, same formula and steps.

facts: Replace x by 1/x and solve the pair: f(x) = (2/x - x - 5)/3
questions.reason: No served row solves a functional equation for f(x) before integrating it.

facts: For x, y >= 0, |x| + |y| = 1 is the line x + y = 1
area under it from 0 to 1 = 1/2 (a triangle)

Bank rows read order and degree from equations that are already polynomial in the derivatives; none clears a square root or a fractional power first. Row ddbac3ae even keys a square-root equation as degree not defined, which is the opposite of the convention this item uses.

facts: integrate: y^2 - x^2 = C, a family of hyperbolas

facts: e^(3x+4y) = e^(3x) e^(4y); separate: e^(-4y) dy = e^(3x) dx

separable initial value problem with an exponential solution

questions.reason: Bank rows solve separable initial value problems by the same steps; splitting e^(3x+4y) into a product is the added step.

facts: Three coins: 8 equally likely outcomes; number of heads 0, 1, 2, 3 with probabilities 1/8, 3/8, 3/8, 1/8
3H or 3T = 1/4; at least two heads = 1/2; at most two heads = 7/8; no head = 1/8

adds point probabilities to get P(X > 2) and P(X <= 2)

questions.reason: Bank row lists the distribution of heads in three tosses; each of the four answers is a sum of those probabilities, which the second row practises.

facts: >= and <= include the boundary line; > and < exclude it

Bank rows test listed relations for reflexive and symmetric, but no served row lists a relation from a rule and gives its domain and range (statements A and B).
